text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government will delay local government elections, which were initially scheduled for November 1995, indefinately because it does not have the resources to hold them now, the electoral commission said.
- Police in the southern town of Choma on Saturday smashed an organised ivory racket and impounded 56 elephant tusks. Three suspects were arrested.

- Germany has finally released $21 million to the Zambian government as its aid allocation for 1996. The allocation was held up because of differences over constitutional reforms the government effected early this year.
- About 70 percent of Zambians are living in absolute poverty, a World Bank report says.
- The Zambia National Union of Farmers has urged to government to exempt farmers from paying a fuel levy if food prices are to be kept low.
